summary_html: **CAPTA §5106a(c)** requires every state to maintain **Citizen Review Panels** that evaluate CPS policies. Project Milk Carton checks whether panels are active, independent, and publicly reporting.

key_cases.case_name: Fosselman v. Commissioner of Human Services
key_cases.holding: The court held that maltreatment-based disqualification proceedings against mandated reporters are subject to procedural due process and that making the commissioner's reconsideration the final agency action, with no evidentiary hearing, denied relators due process.
key_cases.relevance: It supplies the due-process baseline any Minnesota review body must meet when it makes adverse maltreatment findings about individuals.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that disqualification proceedings are subject to the requirements of procedural due process.

key_cases.case_name: Hennepin County Community Services Department v. Hale
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the Commissioner of Administration's order requiring the county to correct a social-services report, holding substantial evidence supported the conclusion that the report was inaccurate in finding the abuse allegation substantiated.
key_cases.relevance: It illustrates independent review of county child-protection determinations outside the juvenile court system.
key_cases.quote: there is substantial evidence in the record to support the Commissioner's decision that the contested report was inaccurate in concluding that the report of abuse by Johnston was substantiated

state_agency.name: Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the county or Tribal child protection agency where the child lives — the directory link is on dcyf.mn.gov/individuals-and-families/report-abuse

timeline_requirements.deadline: Accepted without delay — no waiting period; if the child is determined to be missing and endangered the agency must immediately enter the child into NCIC
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Report of a missing child made to a law enforcement agency
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Minn. Stat. § 299C.53; subd. 1(a) bars a law enforcement agency from refusing a missing person report because the person has been missing only a short time or because the disappearance may be voluntary.
